TELUS (TSX: T, NYSE: TU) is a world-leading communications technology company operating in more than 45 countries and generating over $20 billion in annual revenue with more than 21 million customer connections through our advanced suite of broadband services for consumers, businesses and the public sector. We are committed to leveraging our technology to enable remarkable human outcomes. TELUS is passionate about putting our customers and communities first, leading the way globally in client service excellence and social capitalism. TELUS Health is enhancing more than 161 million lives across 200 countries and territories through innovative preventive medicine and well-being technologies. TELUS Agriculture & Consumer Goods utilizes digital technologies and data insights to optimize the connection between producers and consumers. TELUS Digital specializes in digital customer experiences and future-focused digital transformations that deliver value for their global clients. Guided by our enduring ‘give where we live’ philosophy, TELUS continues to invest in initiatives that support education, health and community well-being. In 2023, we launched the TELUS Student Bursary, which strives to ensure that every young person in Canada who wants a postsecondary education has the opportunity to pursue one. To date, the program has distributed over $6 million in bursaries to 2,000 students and counting. Since 2000, TELUS, our team members and retirees have contributed $1.85 billion in cash, in-kind contributions, time and programs, including 2.5 million days of service—earning TELUS the distinction of the world’s most giving company. Program or Policy: Gas Utilities Act The potential of hydrogen as a low-carbon energy source is significant, however, it is imperative that we implement strategies to keep costs low for individuals and commercial entities alike to ensure widespread adoption of this fuel. The CHA and the Ministry of Affordability and Utilities discussed the Government of Alberta's exploration of policy options and legislative amendments to the Gas Utilities Act to better enable hydrogen within the Alberta utilities system. During the discussion, the potential outcomes and implications of various policy options were examined, alongside the challenges and intricate complexities involved in effectively integrating hydrogen into the utilities system. Information on Ontario and Nova Scotia's experiences in integrating hydrogen within their utility systems was shared by the CHA. Subject Matter Details Post-secondary Education Grant MacEwan University Alberta Advanced Education Financial Benefit or Grant: Campus Mental Health Grant We are advocating for an increase to the Campus Mental Health Grant, at a rate of $188 per FLE, as well as the renewal of the Indigenous Post-Secondary Student Mental Health Grant. The University of Lethbridge was granted $147 per Full Load Equivalent (FLE) in 2013, in accordance with the Campus Mental Health Grant, and drastically reduced the waiting lists for their services. Similar funding, adjusted for the current inflation rate and tied to CPI, guarantees timely and effective mental health access across Alberta’s PSIs. While increased funding for increased access to services may not fully solve systemic mental health issues, it plays a significant role in supporting students during times of crisis. In 2017, the Government of Alberta approved a set of seven actions as Next Steps to Improve Post-secondary Student Mental Health. This included funding for a targeted program, the Indigenous Post Secondary Student Mental Health Grant, which sought to "ensure more Indigenous students have the option to use, and have available, culturally appropriate mental health care and literacy opportunities that acknowledge the historical, colonial, assimilative, and socio-economic factors that impact them. The Grant will also improve Indigenous students’ access to traditional ways of maintaining and healing Organization Lobbyist Registration - Notice of Change Page 7/9 their mental health." While this grant is not currently active, its renewal would work to support efforts around reconciliation. Financial Benefit or Grant: Enhanced funding for sexual and gender based violence prevention We are meeting with Advanced Education and Status of Women to advocate for better funding for SGBV prevention at Alberta's post secondaries. Our asks are: Dedicate sustainable and long-term funding to support survivors of sexual and gender-based violence at Alberta’s post-secondaries Such funding would be distributed to support: Existing on-campus sexual assault responses and/or services, particularly those with identified needs for increased staffing and/or resource-based support; Enhanced access to such services with appropriate funding for coordination with specialized sexual assault services and/or staff at institutions who have expressed a need for their development; Digital programming with accessible, easy to understand language on effectively supporting survivors, managing disclosures, and utilizing trauma- informed practices, to be distributed to institutions across Alberta for use by faculty, staff, and students; Funding for community-based sexual assault supports and centres in contexts where post-secondary students primarily rely on community resources for such care, such as at smaller institutions and rural institutions. Financial Benefit or Grant: Indigenous Student Funding and Honouring Treaties We are meeting with Ministers Wilson and Sawhney on establishing additional financial supports for Indigenous Students provincially. Create additional scholarships for Indigenous students not eligible for band funding, focusing on bursaries and scholarships for self identified Indigenous students, with wider eligibility in regards to programs/disciplines of study, and eligible schools.  2. Serving as a support program for those who have been in foster care, of which 74% are Indigenous, the Advancing Futures program offers a maximum of $40,000 for current and former youth in government care aged 18 to 24. Financial Benefit or Grant: New Beginnings Bursary We are meeting with the Minister of Advanced Education and MLAs to ask for improved funding for student financial aid, specifically the New Beginnings Bursary. Program or Policy: Summer Temporary Employment Program We are advocating for a return of the STEP program. Previously, Alberta's Summer Temporary Employment Program (STEP) provided valuable training to Alberta's students, and supported local businesses in meeting key labour demands. Each summer, roughly 3000 Albertan students benefited from STEP. Introducing a similar program would support students in receiving job training, help fill labour demands, and create the opportunity for students to gain extra income. The Association is fully funded by dues paid by its active member teachers employed by Alberta's public, separate and francophone school authorities with additional revenues coming from associate member fees, rental of space to tenants at Barnett House (the Association's Edmonton office building), casual rental of meeting space and provision of catering services, conference registration fees, sale (typically at cost of production) of publications, sale of advertising in Association publications, most notably the ATA News and ATA Magazine. The Alberta Hotel & Lodging Association (AHLA) is a non-profit organization founded in 1919 that represents the interests of Alberta’s hotel industry. Their purpose is to bring together Alberta hotels to help their members prosper. The AHLA represents over 75% of guest rooms in the province. Their members are owners and operators of more than 650 hotels, motels, inns, resorts, and lodges in communities around Alberta.  The AHLA is also the official health & safety association for all hotels and convention centres in the province. Alberta hotels are at the center of communities across Alberta – they are family owned and operated, employing over 20,000 Albertans. Alberta hotels are in the business of people, serving guests and providing lifelong careers for employees. We are drivers of economic diversification, job creation and sustainable, clean growth.
